This crushed Generative Yield from 15 → 10.84, violating Newton-mode §18 minimum (≥15). v1.1 restores Generative Yield to 15 and rebalances the other originals to maintain sum=100, preserving the M-Form additions intact. Iatrogenic risk note: GP-105's automatic rebalancing logic should be patched to preserve Newton-mode Generative Yield ≥15 invariant.
rubric_mode_reason: gp152 is a self-prompting architectural audit asking the apparatus to design the optimal pre-solver representation-search Framer. Newton-mode is required: the thesis must propose a CLASS of generalizable transformation behaviors and pre-commit to numerical predictions on test cases, not merely describe a single API.
enable_dag_steering_reason: DAG steering keeps the audit anchored on the bipartite-optimization framing (collapse phase + shape phase) rather than drifting into general representation-learning side quests.

farther_tail_region_disable_reason: qualitative architectural audit — no numerical curve to extrapolate.
disable_evidence_fit_gate_reason: qualitative audit — evidence is architectural-map description, not a numerical curve; global_evidence_fit gate does not apply.
disable_uniqueness_gap_gate_reason: qualitative audit — rival Framer designs scored by rubric criteria; mathematical-form keyword heuristic does not apply.

Architectural audits cycle through many distinct critique classes (algorithmic complexity, MDL formalization, integration concreteness, complexity-bound rigor); fine-grained class-novelty preserves the cycling that produces champions.
structural_blocker_enforcement_reason: Task 22 / GP-151 hardkill retirement: deterministic post-champion gates (G-CIRC DAG-cycle detection + G-FALSIFY numeric-assertion + watch_signal + rival check) replace the LLM-taxonomy hardkill prompt injection. The catalog injection is suppressed when this flag is 'gate'. Architectural audits are particularly suited to gate-mode because they're vulnerable to circularity (Framer-to-find-Framer) and unfalsifiability (vague prose); deterministic detection is cleaner than prompt-level warnings.
persona: You are an adversarial software architect with Charlie Munger's inversion discipline and Karl Popper's falsification discipline. You are evaluating proposals for a pre-solver representation-search 'Framer' phase that systematically transforms data coordinates before the main solvers engage. You REJECT: (a) Framer designs that require operator-supplied coordinate hints; (b) Framers that propose brute-force enumeration over O(N!) representation spaces without complexity bounds; (c) Framers that conflate the bipartite optimization (collapse phase + shape phase) and try to fit the law and the transformation simultaneously; (d) Framers without explicit MDL/BIC selection pressure; (e) thesis prose that describes 'what a Framer should do' without naming module paths, hand-off contracts, or numerical predictions on the charter's two test cases. You REWARD: (i) substantive Munger inversions (not 'we wouldn't run the Framer') that derive the design from a structural failure-mode argument; (ii) hierarchical/MDL-prunable transformation spaces with named complexity bounds (e.g., 'O(M log M) per axis with greedy MDL local search'); (iii) explicit symmetry-detection and dimensional-analysis pre-filters that eliminate transformation candidates BEFORE MDL ranking; (iv) named module paths with one-paragraph implementation specs; (v) numerical predictions on the charter's test case A (single dataset, true law y=exp(x²)/(1+log(x))) and test case B (multi-dataset universality collapse).

dimensions.name: Inversion Proof of Current Architecture Failure
dimensions.description: Does the thesis include a substantive Munger inversion proving why ZTARE's current architecture fails to recover f(log(x), 1/y)=C at acceptable parsimony? (a) 0/20 if no inversion or trivial restatement ('the solvers don't transform coordinates'). (b) 8/20 if inversion is non-trivial but doesn't connect to a structural failure mode (e.g., grammar tier limitation, MDL blindness, or basis incompleteness). (c) 14/20 if inversion identifies one specific structural failure mode with mechanism. (d) 20/20 if inversion identifies a CLASS of physical invariants (not just one example) that the current architecture provably misses, with a parsimony-cost argument quantifying the high-parameter penalty in native coordinates.

dimensions.name: Framer Architecture: Complexity Bounds + Hierarchy
dimensions.description: Does the proposed Framer have explicit, polynomial-or-better complexity bounds and a hierarchical/prunable structure? (a) 0/20 for unbounded brute-force enumeration. (b) 8/20 for bounded but flat (single-level) enumeration. (c) 14/20 for hierarchical with named pruning criterion. (d) 20/20 for hierarchical, MDL-prunable, with explicit complexity bound (e.g., 'O(M·log(M)) per axis at depth 1, O(M²·log(M)) at depth 2 conditional on depth-1 MDL improvement'). Symmetry-detection and dimensional-analysis pre-filters that eliminate ≥50% of candidates before MDL ranking earn full credit.

dimensions.name: MDL Integration Rigor
dimensions.description: Does the Framer use Minimum Description Length (or BIC) as the selection pressure, with each MDL component (data dispersion, transformation description length, law description length) explicitly defined and computable? (a) 0/15 if MDL is vaguely invoked without a concrete formula. (b) 8/15 if the MDL formula is stated but components are not computable from the data alone (e.g., 'L_law' is hand-waved). (c) 15/15 if all three MDL components have explicit, computable formulas with named approximations (e.g., BIC for L_law, Kolmogorov-complexity proxy for L_model).

dimensions.name: Generative Yield (Newton-mode)
dimensions.description: Does the thesis pre-commit to numerical predictions on the charter's two test cases? (a) 0/15 if no numerical predictions. (b) 7/15 if predictions on test case A only OR predictions are qualitative ('MDL improvement is large'). (c) 12/15 if both test cases have specific predictions but tolerances are vague. (d) 15/15 if both test cases have specific numerical predictions with declared tolerances (e.g., 'test A: MDL bit-savings ≥ 30 bits at N=200, σ=0.01; test B: residual dispersion floor ≤ 1.5σ on the master curve'). The Newton-mode discipline forbids a thesis that only restates the test cases without numerical commitment.

dimensions.name: Code-Level Concreteness
dimensions.description: Does the thesis name specific module paths, hand-off contracts, and one-paragraph implementation specs per Framer component? (a) 0/10 for verbal descriptions only. (b) 5/10 for some module paths but no hand-off contract. (c) 10/10 for all components named with file paths AND one-paragraph specs AND a concrete hand-off contract to the existing Phase C entry point (`autoresearch_loop.py` or `compress_champion.py`).

dimensions.name: Universality-Collapse Treatment
dimensions.description: Does the thesis explicitly address the multi-dataset universality-collapse extension? (a) 0/10 if unaddressed. (b) 5/10 if mentioned but no architectural commitment ('this could be extended later'). (c) 10/10 if the thesis EITHER (i) shows that the single-dataset Framer subsumes the multi-dataset case as N=1 special case with rigorous reduction, OR (ii) explains why multi-dataset requires its own primitive and bounds the additional complexity cost (≤ 4-week implementation, with named bipartite-optimization core).

dimensions.name: Popper Falsifier Pre-Registration
dimensions.description: Does the thesis pre-register a class of invariants the proposed Framer would still miss, OR a complexity threshold beyond which the Framer becomes intractable? (a) 0/10 for no falsifier. (b) 5/10 for a vague falsifier ('the Framer might miss exotic cases'). (c) 10/10 for a specific named class (e.g., 'invariants of the form f(x·log(y), y/sqrt(x)) require depth-3 composition; the Framer's depth-2 cap rejects them by construction'), and a complexity threshold (e.g., 'with N transformations on each axis, depth-2 enumeration scales as O(N²·M)' where M is dataset size).

dimensions.name: M-Form Charter Alignment: universality_and_pred_tests
dimensions.description: [GP-105 General Office insertion] Theses must rigorously address the multi-dataset universality-collapse extension—detailing the Framer's architecture, expected integration path, and providing quantitative predictions specific to multi-dataset alignment scenarios as described in the charter. Additionally, theses must pre-commit to explicit numerical predictions in both single-dataset and multi-dataset test cases, quantifying expected MDL improvement and residual error/floor. Gap detected: The thesis omits the required universality-collapse extension: it does not design (or rule out) the case where multiple datasets must be aligned onto a single master curve, nor does it discuss or predict the Framer's behavior in multi-dataset alignment. The thesis also does not provide explicit numerical predictions for Test Case A (bit-savings under MDL) or Test Case B (predicted residual dispersion floor for multi-dataset case), as mandated by the charter's secondary observable.

dimensions.name: M-Form Charter Alignment: universality_collapse_coverage
dimensions.description: [GP-105 General Office insertion] Award zero credit unless the thesis explicitly addresses both single-dataset and multi-dataset (universality collapse) scenarios, providing architectural detail, integration plan, and at least one concrete falsifiable numerical prediction for each case. Gap detected: The thesis fails to clearly address the full universality-collapse extension required in the charter: it does not specify a design or falsification mechanism for aligning multiple datasets onto a master curve before committing coordinates, nor does it furnish explicit methodology or numerical prediction for Test Case B (multi-dataset universality collapse). This leaves a major portion of the charter—designing and evaluating the Framer’s behavior in the multi-dataset context—insufficiently engaged.

dimensions.name: M-Form Charter Alignment: universality_collapse_required
dimensions.description: [GP-105 General Office insertion] Theses must (a) explicitly design the multi-dataset universality-collapse extension (not merely cite or mention it), covering algorithmic steps for aligning and scaling N datasets onto a master curve, and (b) provide a numerical prediction for the residual dispersion/floor on a representative test case as in the charter. Failure to both design and numerically forecast the universality-collapse yields a severe penalty. Gap detected: The thesis does not clearly engage the universality-collapse extension in sufficient depth: it mentions multi-dataset universality collapse in passing, but provides neither a concrete design nor discusses the explicit algorithmic steps, architectural hand-off, or failure modes in the multi-dataset alignment/curve collapse scenario. The required predictive numerical outcome (residual dispersion floor, master-curve scaling) for test case B is also missing or insufficiently specified. The rest of the requirements (inversion proof, single-dataset numerical prediction, Framer architecture) are addressed, but the multi-dataset/curve universality-collapse scenario—explicitly demanded in the primary observable and secondary observable—was not concretely developed.

dimensions.name: M-Form Charter Alignment: multi_dataset_universality_alignment
dimensions.description: [GP-105 General Office insertion] Thesis must describe, implement, or rule out the procedures by which the Framer aligns multiple datasets onto a single master curve prior to coordinate commitment. The solution must name or formalize the multi-dataset alignment mechanism and offer a concrete behavioral prediction for universality collapse test cases. Gap detected: The thesis provides a formal inversion showing grammar/solver limitations, describes a Framer with symmetry/MDL, and commits to numerical predictions for iteration savings. However, it does not clearly address or design a universality-collapse extension for the multi-dataset case (i.e., coordinating alignment of N datasets onto a master curve before coordinate commitment), which the charter explicitly requires. There is no detailed proposal or substantial engagement with the multi-dataset transformation/alignment logic, nor is the test case B prediction shown within the visible thesis excerpt.

criteria.Inversion_Proof_of_Current_Architecture_: Inversion must name (a) a specific architectural component (grammar tier, basis function library, MDL-blindness in compress_champion, etc.) AND (b) the structural reason this component cannot represent f(log(x), 1/y)=C at parsimony cost ≤ K parameters for K ≤ 5. A high-parameter polynomial fit in native coords (e.g., 12+ parameters) versus a 1-parameter fit in transformed coords is the canonical evidence; thesis must cite or derive this gap.
criteria.Framer_Architecture:_Complexity_Bounds_+: Explicit complexity bound stated as a function of (M = number of candidate transformations per axis, N = dataset size, D = composition depth, P = number of parameters in the fitted law). Brute-force O(M^D) without pruning fails. Acceptable: O(M·log(M)·N) per depth level with MDL-greedy pruning between levels.
criteria.MDL_Integration_Rigor: The MDL formula must split into at least three terms (data, transformation, law) and each must be computable WITHOUT knowing the true law f. Standard substitutions: BIC for law description length; AST node count or character length for transformation description length; local-variance estimator for data dispersion in Phase 1 (collapse) and standard fit residual in Phase 2 (shape).
criteria.Generative_Yield_(Newton-mode): Test case A: y = exp(x²)/(1 + log(x)), x ∈ [1, 10], N=200, σ=0.01 noise. Predict the MDL bit-savings (transformed vs native) and declare a tolerance. Test case B: two datasets y_i = A_i · x^α + B_i with shared α but different (A_i, B_i). Predict the residual dispersion floor on the master curve.
criteria.Code-Level_Concreteness: At minimum: (1) Framer entry point (e.g., `src/ztare/fit/framer/run_framer.py`); (2) symmetry-detector module; (3) dimensional-analysis module; (4) MDL-greedy search module; (5) Phase-C handoff contract (e.g., 'returns transformed (x, y) arrays + transformation_log JSON'). Each component: one-paragraph spec.
criteria.Universality-Collapse_Treatment: Either (i) reduce single-dataset Framer to multi-dataset N=1 case with rigorous reduction proof, OR (ii) name the bipartite-optimization core (e.g., 'minimize sum of within-cluster local variance over scaling parameters', with optimizer choice: Nelder-Mead / simulated annealing / proximal gradient) and bound implementation cost.
criteria.Popper_Falsifier_Pre-Registration: Named class of physical invariants that the Framer's structural choices (depth cap, transformation library, MDL approximation) cannot recover. Plus: complexity threshold (in big-O notation as a function of named parameters) beyond which the Framer becomes intractable for typical hardware budgets.
criteria.mform_universality_and_pred_tests: Theses must rigorously address the multi-dataset universality-collapse extension—detailing the Framer's architecture, expected integration path, and providing quantitative predictions specific to multi-dataset alignment scenarios as described in the charter. Additionally, theses must pre-commit to explicit numerical predictions in both single-dataset and multi-dataset test cases, quantifying expected MDL improvement and residual error/floor.
criteria.mform_universality_collapse_coverage: Award zero credit unless the thesis explicitly addresses both single-dataset and multi-dataset (universality collapse) scenarios, providing architectural detail, integration plan, and at least one concrete falsifiable numerical prediction for each case.
criteria.mform_universality_collapse_required: Theses must (a) explicitly design the multi-dataset universality-collapse extension (not merely cite or mention it), covering algorithmic steps for aligning and scaling N datasets onto a master curve, and (b) provide a numerical prediction for the residual dispersion/floor on a representative test case as in the charter. Failure to both design and numerically forecast the universality-collapse yields a severe penalty.
criteria.mform_multi_dataset_universality_alignme: Thesis must describe, implement, or rule out the procedures by which the Framer aligns multiple datasets onto a single master curve prior to coordinate commitment. The solution must name or formalize the multi-dataset alignment mechanism and offer a concrete behavioral prediction for universality collapse test cases.
